summary_paragraph: A woman with idiopathic chronic pancreatitis was admitted for an acute flare characterized by worsening epigastric pain radiating to the back, nausea, and vomiting. She had been on home TPN due to inability to tolerate oral intake. An MRCP was performed to rule out pseudocyst or pancreatic cancer, which showed chronic pancreatitis changes with a nearly normal secretin response and no concerning lesions. Her PICC line was found to be malpositioned and was replaced fluoroscopically. She was managed with bowel rest, TPN, IV fluids, and pain and nausea control. As symptoms improved, she was transitioned to oral hydromorphone and Phenergan suppositories, and her diet was advanced. Gabapentin was discontinued due to lack of efficacy. She was discharged home with ongoing TPN, saline infusions for dehydration, visiting nurse support, and follow-up with gastroenterology.
